draft.title: Terrorism and the response
card: On 11 September 2001, al-Qaeda hijacked four passenger planes and attacked targets in the United States. Nearly 3000 people died. Al-Qaeda was a militant network led by Osama bin Laden.
President George W. Bush declared a "war on terror". The US wanted to stop terrorist groups and the states that sheltered them.
The Taliban government sheltered al-Qaeda and refused to hand over bin Laden. In October 2001 a US-led coalition invaded and removed the Taliban from power.

The US, with the UK, Australia and others, invaded Iraq and removed Saddam Hussein. The main reason given was the claim that Iraq held weapons of mass destruction. Such weapons were not found, and the war was widely criticised.
draft.remember: After 9/11 the US fought a war on terror: first in Afghanistan, then in Iraq.

a.q: Why did a US-led coalition invade Afghanistan in October 2001?
opts: The Taliban government sheltered al-Qaeda after 9/11
Afghanistan's government had attacked the United States
Afghanistan was said to hold weapons of mass destruction
The Taliban government had invaded a neighbouring state
a.why: The Taliban sheltered al-Qaeda, which carried out the 9/11 attacks, and would not hand over bin Laden. The weapons of mass destruction claim was the main reason given for the Iraq invasion in 2003, not for Afghanistan.
a.clue: Think about who was living under the Taliban's protection.

b.q: Which statement best describes the invasion of Iraq in 2003?
opts: A war based on a claim about weapons that were not found
A response to Iraq's role in planning the 9/11 attacks
A campaign to remove the Taliban from power in Iraq
A peacekeeping mission that the whole UN had endorsed
b.why: The main reason given was that Iraq held weapons of mass destruction, and none were found. The Taliban ruled Afghanistan, not Iraq, so removing them belongs to the 2001 war. The card does not link Iraq to the planning of 9/11.
b.clue: Recall the main reason given for the war, and what became of it.

a.best: The Taliban government sheltered al-Qaeda after 9/11

b.best: A war based on a claim about weapons that were not found

problems.detail: Why (b) dismisses the 9/11-planning option only because 'the card does not link Iraq to the planning of 9/11'. This hints that a link might exist but simply isn't covered. It should say plainly that Iraq had no role in planning 9/11 (the 9/11 Commission found no operational link), so students don't take the wrong option as merely untaught.

check.summary: The facts and answers check out. Why (b) should state that Iraq had no role in 9/11, rather than saying only that the card does not mention one.
